messages:
sarah: FYI starting a lightweight probe for envelope_v3 — introduce a shared string_dictionary table + compact payload refs to dedupe repeated keys/values in telemetry events. synthetic runs show ~45% reduction in payload bytes. looking for read-adapter tradeoff feedback and a rollout sketch.
ben: cool. are we going to keep envelope_v2 reads available? how do we handle legacy dashboard queries?
max: plan should be dual-write initially + a read_adapter that materializes the old JSON shape on the fly. minimizes changes to consumers.
olivia: my main concern is dashboard p99. JSONB -> dict-refs requires extra joins/lookups; could blow up p95/p99 for ad-hoc queries.
sarah: agreed. proposed phased approach: 1) dual-write (v2 JSONB + v3 compact) 2) route console reads through read_adapter with a bounded lookup cache 3) gradual cutover with per-route feature flags and a safe retention window before v2 deletion.
leo: sketch the read_adapter caching model? in-process sharded cache or an external LRU (memcached/redis)?
sarah: prototype uses sharded in-process LRU with async refresh and batch id lookups. rough SQL and shapes pasted below. batch lookup cap is 200 ids to avoid spikes.
```sql
-- new schema
CREATE TABLE string_dictionary (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, value text);
CREATE TABLE envelope_v3 (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, ts timestamptz, dict_refs jsonb, route_id text, raw_size_est int);
-- dict_refs example: {"keys": [{"k":"event_kind","ids":["id1"]}, {"k":"ua","ids":["id2","id3"]}]}
```
read_adapter flow: if payload compact -> gather ids, batch SELECTs to string_dictionary, reconstruct to JSONB. small payload shortcut: inline reconstruction if <512 bytes.
ben: batch lookups ok but watch dict_miss storms. need circuit breaker or sampling fallback to JSONB read.
max: suggest a prefix-hot cache for high-cardinality fields we query often (route_name, event_kind, country) with 1h TTL. keeps p95 low for dashboards.
olivia: dashboard owners need a hard fallback that returns original JSONB shape while we evaluate performance. ETL teams: we must update downstream Kusto mapping or keep current ETL until cutover.
sarah: ETL approach: keep existing extractor working off v2 for now. add a lightweight transformer that can emit exploded rows from v3 for analytics consumers; enable when ready.
leo: billing concerns: smaller storage is great but cost accounting must not change unexpectedly for customers. add a migration header so cost is computed from v2 until we flip.
ben: yep. maintain a tokens+payload_size header during dual-write window. switch accounting to v3-computed size only after a safety window.
max: what about backfilling historical envelopes into v3? that's going to be the ops heavy lift.
sarah: backfill plan: streaming transformer reading v2, writing v3 with idempotency checks (checksums). run at controlled throughput per-region with concurrency gating and per-tenant pause. backfill is toggleable and resumable.
olivia: ops/runbook requests: publish abort criteria and a dashboard with: read_latency_p95, dict_lookup_p95, dual_write_error_rate, backfill_progress, per-route read errors.
sarah: drafting runbook. abort criteria proposal: sustained read p95 > 2x baseline for 10m OR dual_write_error_rate > 0.5% for 15m OR backfill error_rate > 1% for 30m.
leo: rollout plan: canary on an internal low-traffic tenant, then open to 5-10% customers via routing policy. include per-route feature flag so large customers can opt-out.
ben: also add a region-level pause for backfill and a console toggle for SRE to pause/resume.
max: I'll add adapter metrics (cache_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram, lookup_latency) and tracing spans to pinpoint hot keys.
olivia: I'll own docs and ETL mapping changes + a note on raw JSON retention (v2 raw JSON will be available for 30 days only after cutover). update query examples in the telemetry docs.
sarah: timeline: probe + read_adapter prototype this week, dual-write in staging next week, small canary in 2 weeks, broader ramp over 4 weeks with backfill running concurrently. will open PRs for schemas, adapter, and backfill tool.
eng-platform-bot: sarah added checklist: prototype_read_adapter, dual_write_migration, backfill_tool, runbook, dashboards, per-route_feature_flag. @here
ben: ack, will review schema PR and cost-accounting change.
max: I'll help with instrumentation and performance benching.
olivia: I'll coordinate ETL owners and update docs.
sarah: thanks all — will post RFC + PR links when ready.
